validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION: real and well documented. Independent sources: (1) SEC EDGAR — Regency Energy Partners LP FY2005 10-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1338613/000095013406006440/d34351e10vk.htm), the applicant's own regulatory financial disclosure, describing the 'Regency Intrastate Pipeline system' in north Louisiana as a Transportation-segment asset distinct from Regency's Gathering & Processing segment; (2) Energy Transfer's current operator page (https://www.energytransfer.com/ops_intrastate.aspx) lists 'RIGS Haynesville Partnership Co.' among its active intrastate systems today ('RIGS is a 450-mile intrastate pipeline that delivers natural gas from northwest Louisiana to downstream pipelines and markets', capacity 2.1 Bcf/d — a SYSTEM-level current figure, not this row's); (3) offshore-technology.com/GlobalData infrastructure database (2021/2022, via Wayback since the live host 403s scripted clients: https://web.archive.org/web/20251009172935/https://www.offshore-technology.com/marketdata/regency-intrastate-system-gas-pipeline-the-us/) independently lists a '724km-long Regency Intrastate System' operated by 'RIGS Haynesville Partnership'; (4) a Louisiana 2nd Circuit Court of Appeal contract-dispute opinion, Regency Intrastate Gas, L.L.C. v. Caddo Gas Gathering, L.L.C. (2009) (https://web.archive.org/web/20250210050013/https://caselaw.findlaw.com/court/la-court-of-appeal/1504234.html), independently confirms Regency owns and operates a gas-transportation pipeline in the Caddo Parish area, tracing chain of title back through 'Gulf States Gas Corporation' to a 1988 lease of the 'Elm Grove Pipeline System' from Southwestern Electric Power Company (SWEPCO). None of these are GEM/wiki, abarrelfull, or theodora. Classification as a gas transmission/transportation pipeline (not gathering) matches the operator's own segment reporting, even though the assembly GEM tracks under this name includes some small-diameter (6-in, 4-in) 'Ruston System' laterals per the 10-K's itemized component list — those read more like gathering interconnects than trunk pipe, but Regency itself books the whole assembly under 'Transportation', so I did not raise this as a hard classification concern. OWNERSHIP/OPERATOR: CSP Daily News (http://www.cspdailynews.com/fuels-news-prices-analysis/fuels-news/articles/etp-regency-complete-merger — does NOT name the pipeline itself, name_found=false, so this is corroborating corporate context only, not a standalone [ref]-worthy source) confirms Energy Transfer Partners LP and Regency Energy Partners LP completed their merger April 30, 2015, with Regency becoming a wholly-owned ETP subsidiary — consistent with the sheet's Owner1 = 'ETP Legacy' and with Energy Transfer's website today listing RIGS as one of its own intrastate systems. DUPLICATE CHECK vs roster: P5823 is also labeled 'Regency Intrastate Gas (RIGS) Pipeline' (len=120mi, dia=30/42in, cap=600 MMcf/d) — this is NOT a duplicate to merge; it matches the 2005 'Regency Intrastate Enhancement Project' (40-mile 24-in loop + 80-mile 30-in Winnsboro extension = 120 mi, +600 MMcf/d bringing system capacity from 200→800 MMcf/d) described in the same 10-K, i.e. a genuine second construction phase of the same physical network, not a relabeled copy of P0244. Opened/read to exhaustion: gem.wiki page (leads only, never cited), the full 10-K text (searched for every numeric claim on this row), the ET intrastate page, the offshore-technology snapshot, the 2008 NGI article, the FindLaw opinion, and the Google Books EIS snippet (East Texas to Mississippi Expansion Project FEIS, FERC May 2007 — snippet-view only, confirms an unrelated 'Regency Pipeline' 80-mile 30-in project appears in a THIRD-PARTY FERC EIS for a different pipeline's expansion, i.e. FERC's own environmental review independently corroborates the 80-mile/30-in Enhancement Project component — but Google Books snippet view would not render enough text to extract a clean citable quote/URL, so I did not stage it as a [ref]; noting it here per the read-to-exhaustion rule).

validity.recommendation: downgrade Length confidence / re-derive: the 10-K's own itemized pre-enhancement component breakdown sums to ~147.5 mi, ~52 mi short of the sheet's 200 mi
validity.researcher_notes: Capacity=200.00 MMcf/d is LITERALLY stated in the 10-K: 'increased our capacity on the Regency Intrastate Pipeline from 200 MMcf/d to 800 MMcf/d' (via the Dec-2005 Enhancement Project) — strong, direct support. Length=200.00 mi, however, is NOT literally stated anywhere in the source; it is only derivable as 320 mi (system total stated post-enhancement) minus ~120 mi of new Enhancement-Project pipe (a 40-mi loop + an 80-mi extension). But the SAME 10-K also itemizes the pre-enhancement system component-by-component: Elm Grove System (31 mi, 12-in, 1974) + North Louisiana Pipeline (23 mi 12-in + 25 mi 16-in, 1989) + Metco Pipeline (19 mi, 20-in, 1990) + Ruston System (12 mi 6-in + 6 mi 12-in + 0.5 mi 4-in) + Panda Pipeline (20 mi 20-in + 11 mi 24-in, 2002) = 147.5 mi total — about 52 mi short of the 200 mi the subtraction implies. This is an internal inconsistency IN THE SOURCE ITSELF (rounding, unlisted laterals/meter stations, or a scope difference between the 'system' figure and the itemized list), not a disagreement between GEM and an independent source, so I stage the 200 mi value (matching GEM's own wiki citation) but at medium tier rather than high, and flag it here for a second source to resolve. Diameter='12, 16, 20, 24' in also only covers the larger components (Elm Grove 12, North LA 12/16, Metco 20, Panda 20/24); it omits the Ruston System's 6-in and 4-in laterals, which the itemized list places inside the same pre-enhancement 'system.' Searched for a second, independent numeric source for the pre-2005 length/diameter total: EIA (naturalgas/data.php is a navigation page per the scope note, not usable as a table citation, and I found no EIA pipeline-project-table row matching this specific pre-2005 baseline), FERC eLibrary (RIGS is Louisiana-intrastate and outside FERC jurisdiction, so FERC silence here is expected per the scope guidance, not an existence concern), and Louisiana DNR/SONRIS (no distinct pipeline-mileage record surfaced for this specific system in the time available). None resolved the ~52-mile gap; Length and Diameter stay medium-tier pending a second primary source.

validity.recommendation: verify EndLocation='Franklin Parish' against the 10-K's own geography; consider whether it belongs on P5823 instead
validity.researcher_notes: The sheet's EndLocation/EndState-Province for P0244 reads Franklin Parish, Louisiana. But per the SAME 10-K GEM cites, the PRE-enhancement system (which is what this row's Length=200mi/Capacity=200 MMcf/d actually describe, per the validity note above) terminates at an interconnection with a Southern Natural Gas Company pipeline IN BIENVILLE PARISH ('the North Louisiana Pipeline ... extends from the tie-in point with the Elm Grove System to an interconnection with a pipeline owned by Southern Natural Gas Company in Bienville Parish'). Franklin Parish only enters the picture via the 2005 Enhancement Project's 80-mile, 30-inch 'Winnsboro extension,' explicitly described as extending 'from the eastern terminus of the North Louisiana Pipeline to a point near Winnsboro, Louisiana' — and Winnsboro is the Franklin Parish seat. Winnsboro/Franklin Parish is P5823's territory (120 mi, 30/42-in, +600 MMcf/d), not the 200-mi/200-MMcf/d segment tracked here. This reads as a likely mix-up: the network's furthest downstream reach (Franklin Parish) may have been attached to the wrong construction-phase row. I did not attempt a fix — this is a judgment call for whoever reconciles P0244 vs P5823's Location cells, and I have not staged a confirming ref for EndLocation because I believe the current value is more likely wrong than right. StartLocation='Caddo Parish' IS well supported (Elm Grove System begins at SWEPCO's Arsenal Hill Power Plant, Caddo Parish, per the 10-K).

validity.recommendation: note in ResearcherNotes that StartYear1=1974 covers only the oldest of ≥5 distinct pipeline components this row aggregates
validity.researcher_notes: The 10-K shows the 'Regency Intrastate Pipeline system' (pre-enhancement, i.e. this row) is actually an assembly of at least five separately built components: Elm Grove System (1974), North Louisiana Pipeline (1989), Metco Pipeline (1990), Ruston System (year not stated in the source), and Panda Pipeline (2002). GEM's single StartYear1=1974 reflects only the earliest (Elm Grove, 31 of ~147.5–200 mi) — a defensible 'earliest in-service' modeling convention for a merged/renamed system, not a fabrication, but worth flagging so a reviewer doesn't read 1974 as the vintage of the whole 200-mile pipe. FuelSource='Haynesville shale' is a genuinely CURRENT-operations fact (the system was rebranded/marketed as 'RIGS Haynesville Partnership Co.' and heavily expanded 2008–2010 specifically to move Haynesville Shale gas — 2008 NGI article: 'Regency Energy Partners LP is planning a $1.1 billion expansion of its Regency Intrastate Gas System in North Louisiana to bring natural gas from the Haynesville Shale to market'; https://naturalgasintel.com/news/regency-energy-partners-to-expand-louisiana-pipeline/), corroborated by the offshore-technology/GlobalData page's operator name 'RIGS Haynesville Partnership.' It is NOT, however, the gas source the 1974–2002-era pre-Haynesville components originally carried — the 10-K's 2005 discussion names Vernon, Elm Grove, and Sligo fields as the system's producing sources at that time, years before Haynesville Shale production existed commercially. FuelSource as currently recorded describes what the (now-integrated, Haynesville-branded) pipeline carries today, which is accurate for an operating-status row, so I staged it rather than flagging a hard concern — but the historical caveat is worth keeping in ResearcherNotes.
